title: Unfamiliar city, well…it’s familiar now
content: I am not sure if I should post this as a reply to my original post about this city or not. Anyway, we got an apartment a while ago that is a walk up with a very flat concrete facade. There’s a side walk that starts near the parking lot and will lead you a circle around a big body of water. Same bodega every day. I pull out left, even know the feeling of the little but before your car leaves the driveway to the road. Then I get to a stop sign a block up. The bodega is on the adjacent corner. Always busy, has food and counter space and cigarettes and what the hell else you need. Still looking for their vet though. I know it’s somewhere. That’s one of the blocks in between the city line to my left and the docks to the right on either sides of the city (I mentioned this aspect of the city and someone I ran into that had ODed and realized I couldn’t have done anything, and I couldn’t carry the guilt of not doing enough. I still cry for him as I speak. But he’s like a ghost there. Living with the hopeless vagabonds). This place feels so real. My friend who has been flakey and becoming more and more of an egomaniac as hell to our friend Matt and I came to visit. He ditched a night at the tea bar with me to do something else. Talk to Matt the next day and he says, “he was in my dream too! In town doing a TED talk”and we are still laughing our asses off over it.
